records.name: The Philadelphia Chorus
records.summary: A community chorus founded in 1951 that holds auditions by appointment and is marking its 75th anniversary with a concert on December 5, 2026.
records.what_you_do: Book an audition by appointment, then sing with the chorus in Monday evening rehearsals and in its concerts. Singers must be 18 or older.

schedule.text: Rehearsals are on Monday evenings in University City.

locations.label: Rehearsals in University City (exact address not on the pages checked)

cost.text: The chorus site says it charges no dues or fees, and the audition page lists no audition fee.

first_step.how: Call 215-995-3118 or email thephiladelphiachorus@gmail.com to book an audition by appointment.
first_step.basis: Joining starts with a booked audition by appointment, which includes a sung test, so the way in is clear but a newcomer cannot watch a rehearsal first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The audition asks you to sing scales and warm-ups, then one song of your choice in any style, and to sight-read a short excerpt. The page does not say how long it takes. Once you join, you rehearse on Monday evenings in University City and sing in concerts each season.
first_visit_tips: Pick a song you know well, and plan on accompaniment if you can, since the chorus prefers it.
When you book, ask how long the audition runs and where rehearsals meet, since the site does not say.
Book a time first. Auditions are by appointment only.

records.notes: Homepage names Raquel García as artistic director and Judith Large as accompanist. Contact page gives a P.O. Box (42735, Philadelphia, PA 19101) and a contact form, with no email published. Rehearsal address and any visitor policy for rehearsals are not published, so ask when booking. Dated events on the group's own pages: a 75th anniversary concert on Saturday, December 5, 2026 at 4 pm at the cathedral, with tickets sold through Eventbrite, and a concert on Saturday, April 10, 2027 at 4 pm at the same venue. The audition page refers to the upcoming season without a year.

records.name: The Phoenix Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit community for people in recovery, the people who love them, and anyone who wants friends without alcohol or drugs. Its Philadelphia programs include workouts, art, social meetups and other free events.
records.what_you_do: Go to free sober activities led by volunteers, such as weekly chair yoga, weekly community yoga, fitness sessions, art, or social meetups. Most listings have a reserve button to hold a spot. To volunteer, the site describes a short process that starts with its NewForm app and includes attending two events first. The group plans a sober community center in North Philadelphia, which the site said would open in spring 2026; the pages checked do not confirm that it has opened.

schedule.text: Weekly chair yoga on Fridays at 10:30 am at Fox Chase Library, and weekly community yoga on Saturdays at 11 am, weather permitting. Other events are posted on the website.

locations.label: Other Philadelphia events (addresses not published on the pages checked)
Community yoga, weekly on Saturdays (in partnership with Historic Fairhill)

cost.text: The website says its programs are free. The yoga listings checked do not name a fee.

access.notes: The chair yoga listing is titled as chair based, but it gives no wheelchair, quiet space, parking or transit details.

first_step.how: Reserve a spot on the Friday chair yoga listing (Fox Chase Library, 10:30 am), or send a question through the Contact Us page on thephoenix.org.
first_step.basis: The site says people seeking connection are welcome whether or not they are in recovery, and the Friday chair yoga is listed for all levels with a reserve button.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Friday chair yoga is 60 minutes, listed for all levels, with 15 spots per listing. The Saturday community yoga is a 60 minute gentle, slow flow class, and mats are provided. The activities are led by volunteers.
first_visit_tips: Reserve your spot on the listing first, since each class lists a limited number of places.
Check the listing before the Saturday class, since it is held weather permitting.
You do not need to bring a mat to the Saturday class, because the listing says mats are provided.

records.notes: The homepage lists Philadelphia events (chair yoga, community yoga, and a trail run) without dates. The explore events page checked the same day lists only events outside the city, so re-check the Philadelphia listings before this goes live. That gap is why status is probably_active and not active. The safety page gives info@thephoenix.org only as a way to raise a concern, so it is not recorded as a general contact. The about page has no Philadelphia details. The chair yoga and community yoga listings are named as the Fox Chase Library and Germantown Avenue events from tier 1.

records.name: The Plastic Club
records.summary: A volunteer-run art club in Center City that has supported artists since 1897. It runs weekly drawing and open studio sessions, monthly art shows, and film, music and poetry nights.
records.what_you_do: Drop in to a weekly drawing or open studio session. Where a fee is listed it is $5 to $10, and most sessions need no booking. You can also apply to join the club as a member: full membership is $60 a year, associate $40, and long distance $25. Artists can enter the club's exhibitions through its open calls.

schedule.text: Sessions run Monday to Saturday, mornings through evenings. Examples: Tuesday 9:30 am to 12:30 pm (clothed portrait model), Thursday 5:30 to 8:30 pm (life model), and Saturday 9:30 am to 12:30 pm (croquis). Printmaking open studio is on Saturdays from 10 am to 2 pm. A Tuesday night Zoom share is also listed.

cost.text: Life model and costume sessions are $10 each ($9 for members, $7 for students). Still life open studio is $5. Printmaking open studio is $10. Some sessions show no fee. Membership: full $60 a year, associate $40, long distance $25.

first_step.how: Read the Guide to Workshop Etiquette on the weekly workshops page, then come to a Thursday or Saturday open studio. New printmaking participants should text 609-682-1088 to book with the monitor first.
first_step.basis: Most workshops need no booking and are open to the public, though new people must read the etiquette guide first, and printmaking needs an appointment and has no beginner class.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most life drawing sessions run about three hours with a model, and the club brings easels, drawing boards and small tables. The page does not say what to bring, so bring your own supplies if you have them. Printmaking is the one session that needs a booking first.
first_visit_tips: Read the Guide to Workshop Etiquette before you come, since every new participant is asked to.
Bring your own drawing supplies, since the page lists only easels, boards and tables from the club.
Masks are optional, but a workshop host or monitor can require one, so check before you come.
No pets are allowed in workshops.

records.notes: The calendar page lists no dated events, and the events and news, upcoming exhibitions and special workshops pages were not re-read in this pass, so dated sessions may be listed there. Weekly workshop and membership fees were re-read today. The mask policy page says masks are optional, a host can require them, and proof of vaccination is not required. The introduction page gives no fees, parking or accessibility details.

records.name: The Primavera Fund
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that mentors young musicians toward top music schools and careers, and helps students with the cost of study. It runs free career sessions for young musicians and keeps an instrument library.
records.what_you_do: Join a free virtual career session for young musicians, or email the fund about the Primavera Artist program. That program requires financial need and at least one year of playing, and the site does not say how to apply. Applications for spring 2026 are closed, and the next round is not dated.

schedule.text: Free virtual career sessions for young musicians, with a registration link posted on the homepage for each one. Session times are not on the site.

locations.label: Mailing address (P.O. Box); sessions are virtual

cost.text: The career sessions are free. The site does not state a cost to artists in the mentoring program.

first_step.how: Watch the homepage for the link to the next free virtual career session, or email rachel@primaverafund.org to ask how to apply to the Primavera Artist program.
first_step.basis: The free career sessions are open to all young musicians with a registration link, but the Primavera Artist program needs financial need, a year of playing and an audition, and its application steps are not posted.
first_step.what_to_expect: The free sessions are virtual, with music professionals presenting and taking questions. The site describes them as a virtual job fair for students. Session times are not on the site. The Primavera Artist program expects weekly private lessons, a weekly orchestra and a smaller ensemble, at least two hours of practice a day, and summer music activities.
first_visit_tips: Know how many years you have played your instrument, since the artist program asks for at least one.
The instrument library is for Primavera Artists, and the site gives no loan terms, so ask by email or phone.
Artist auditions ask for one major scale and its relative minor, then a solo piece, and no accompanist is needed.
Email rachel@primaverafund.org or call (267) 908-1710 to ask about applying, since the steps are not posted.

records.notes: The upcoming events page lists a virtual job fair for students on March 11, March 18 and March 25, but gives no year, so those dates were left out of the record. The apply page says the spring 2026 auditions are closed and tells applicants to prepare for next year without naming the year. The instrument library page gives no deposit, loan length or instrument list. Its office hours are Tuesday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm, and Saturday, 9 am to 1 pm. The get involved page was checked and added nothing new.

records.name: The Print Center
records.summary: A free museum of printmaking and photography in Center City, founded in 1915. It shows changing exhibitions and runs a yearly competition for artists, and paid memberships bring member events and shop discounts.
records.what_you_do: Visit the free galleries during open hours, or book a guided tour, which the site offers for each exhibition and by appointment. Artists can enter The ANNUAL competition. Membership starts at $30 for students and $40 for artists, and the $50 individual level and up includes invitations to members-only events.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11 am to 6 pm, with free admission. Each exhibition has guided tours, and tours can also be booked by appointment.

cost.text: Admission is free. Memberships are optional, from $30 a year for students up to $500 for benefactors. The site does not give a fee for tours.

access.notes: The entry has a step of about 6 inches through a doorway about 31 inches wide. The second floor galleries are reached only by stairs. The first floor restroom is not wheelchair accessible. Seating is limited on both floors. The page gives no details on an elevator, sensory options or ASL.

first_step.how: Come during open hours to see the free galleries, or call 215.735.6090 ext. 1 to book a guided tour by appointment.
first_step.basis: The galleries are free, open to the public and need no sign-up, but the site lists no beginner classes and tours need a call to book.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a walk through the current exhibition, The Long Ride Home about Black cowboys in America, with no sign-up and no admission fee. Exhibition tours run about 30 minutes, and the events page gives their times. If you use a wheelchair, plan around the entry step and the stairs to the second floor.
first_visit_tips: Parking: the museum points to the Academy House Parking Garage at 251 S. 15th Street, about one block away.
Expect limited seating on both floors.
Call 215.735.6090 ext. 1 if you need access details or tour times before you come.

records.notes: The events page lists public exhibition tours on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 12 pm (already past), Friday, October 23, 2026 at 5:30 pm, and Friday, November 13, 2026 at 5:30 pm. Each is about 30 minutes. The events page does not say whether these tours need booking or cost extra. The recorded programs page lists talks by year from 2020 to 2026 and has no beginner classes. The site says some content is temporarily unavailable, so call for access details.

records.name: The Resource Exchange
records.summary: A reuse shop and gallery that sells donated and reclaimed art and craft materials at low prices. It runs workshops, a monthly gallery night and volunteer days, and gives artists a gallery call for work made from its materials.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer day through the sign-up link on the site, join a workshop such as the block printing session, or visit the shop and the gallery night. Artists can apply to the reCreate gallery through its open calls.

schedule.text: The shop and gallery are open Wednesday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and Sunday, noon to 4 pm. The monthly gallery night is on the second Thursday, 5 to 8 pm.

cost.text: The site describes its shop items as low priced, but prices are not shown on the pages checked. Workshop, volunteer and gallery night costs are not listed on the site.

access.notes: The contact page says the shop is easily reached from Berks station on the Market-Frankford subway line, and buses 3 and 57 also serve the area. Free customer parking is in the fenced lot. The page does not say whether entry is step-free or has an elevator, so call first.

first_step.how: Visit the shop at 1800 N. American St during open hours, or use the volunteer sign-up link on the site for the next volunteer day.
first_step.basis: Visitors can walk into the shop and gallery with no sign-up, and volunteer days and workshops use sign-up links, but the site gives no volunteer age limits or workshop costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: A shop visit is a browse through donated and reclaimed art and craft supplies, sold at low prices. The gallery shows work by local artists and makers who use reclaimed materials. Volunteer days and workshops have set times and sign-up links, but the site does not give a general shift length.
first_visit_tips: Free customer parking is in the fenced lot, and the shop sits on the right side toward the north end.
The shop is not listed as open on Monday or Tuesday, so plan for Wednesday to Sunday.
Ask about the cost of a workshop before you sign up, since the site does not show it.

records.notes: The homepage lists a gallery night on October 8, a block printing workshop on October 17, a volunteer day from 11 am to 2 pm on October 24, and a November 10 deadline for the reCreate open call. None of these shows a year, so none was used as evidence. The newest dated evidence is the impact post published January 14, 2026. The volunteer sign-up link is a shortener that redirects to a ticket listing on Eventbrite, a lead only platform, so it was not followed. The page does not say what volunteers do. Workshop and volunteer costs are not published.

records.name: The Savoy Company
records.summary: A Gilbert and Sullivan company formed in 1901 as The Savoy Company of Philadelphia. Its 2026 summer show was staged at a garden in Villanova, and its mailing office is in Norristown.
records.notes: Verdict changed from tier 1 (hide, out_of_scope) to out_of_area. The group does not fall in any out of scope category in the brief. The group calls itself Philadelphia-based, and its history page says its residency venue was the Academy of Music in Philadelphia, with performances each year from 1925 to 2011. Its 2026 season names only Stoneleigh in Villanova and Longwood Gardens, and its only published address is a mailing office in Norristown. No current venue inside the City of Philadelphia was found. This is a borderline call: if the owner counts the greater Philadelphia region as Philadelphia, this should become a publish record. The join page is an interest form, and no audition or crew dates are posted.
